Creates a barrier that blocks one drain attack. Stackable.
Rainbow light hits one foe; stronger per spell cast in battle.
Asks the gods for a mighty miracle at the cost of one level.
Cures one ally of Sleep.
Cures one ally of Silence.
Cures one ally of Confusion.
Cures one ally of Charm.
Cures one ally of Petrification.
Cures one ally of Sleep, Silence, Confusion and Charm.
Gives light; hidden devices are easier to spot. No time limit.
Lifts the curse on spirit and undead monsters.
Creates a barrier that blocks one breath attack. Stackable.
[Instrument] Blesses all allies' weapons so they hit spirits.
[Instrument] Fissure damages foes; low chance to swallow them.
[Instrument] Resets battle stat changes on all friends & foes.
[Servant] Spends all money for limitless damage to one enemy.
Instantly kills one demon-type monster.
Fully heals one ally's HP; cures all ailments but Death/Ash.

Likely the first weapon a Fighter holds. It's called "long" next to the short sword, but isn't really that long. Its length, weight and grip are tuned so even a novice can wield it. It's cheap, but grip it again after using other swords and you'll notice the smith's care. Then you've come of age.

A sword adventurers dream of. Even at low levels it delivers steady power. But that isn't its only draw: the blade is charged with magic, and one stroke sends a wave of flame rushing at the foe. Once it's yours, the danger to watch for may be not the monsters but your own complacency.
A legendary sword said to unleash more power the older its wielder is. Its wooden blade looks flimsy at first glance, but an unseen force lets it cut even through iron.

A sword made to sever the world of the dead from this one. Its task done, it now sleeps quietly. Its aura is the miasma of the underworld, and its blade is said to show every evil deed of this world. Should one without will wield it, they will be cursed and carried off to the land of the dead.

A long spear with a large triangular head. Built to excel at slashing and thrusting, the functions no weapon can do without, it is a spear made purely for attack. The blade makes up nearly all its weight, so slashes that carry that weight are extremely effective.
There are many kinds of axe, and their shapes have changed to suit how they were used. In the orthodox sense, 'axe' means a weapon like this hand axe: a wooden haft fitted with a metal blade.

You beat your foe in a frenzy until they're a bloody mess, and before you know it, only a lump of meat lies there. Delighting in the slick feel of the weapon in your grip, you run your fingers over it endlessly, smiling. Do people create the Blood Hammer, or does the Blood Hammer change people?

Deathdeath pikopiko, bloodshed! Deathdeath pikopiko, boom! Hits hurt, My Darling, but don't run, fall in HELL! I'll haunt you anywhere, love's range cap OFF! (zing!) Deathdeath pikopiko, fresh blood! Deathdeath pikopiko, precious! Even burnt to ash, by love's special POW-WER! I L-O-V-E U...smooch~

This tale tells of a boy raised as a girl and a girl raised as a boy. 'Torikaebaya' is said to be old Eastern for 'I wish I could swap such-and-such.' In the tale, it's the two children's sexes, but I don't think you can just swap those because you want to. A cultural difference, perhaps?
Great Hestrio Hist.

This shield holds holy power and is favored by those who serve the gods, such as Valkyries. Made of light iron, it is light and easy to handle. Light iron is said to break easily, but its durability is not low, perhaps thanks to divine blessing. If your Priest fights up front, give them one.

A helm shaped like an upturned iron bucket. It covers the front down to about the nose and the back down to the nape, a reassuring design for defense. But it badly limits vision, so as a remedy, a horizontal slit is cut at eye level.

Full-body armor made for knights, designed with mounted combat in mind. Knights in national service, except captains, are issued this armor. Its basic performance differs little from Plate Mail, but it is somewhat easier to move in.
Raw meat of the giant creature Airy Vider. The meat is so huge that to bring it back, you must either travel by magic or carry it on your back, roped to your body.

A fallen samurai is an eastern samurai who survived a war on the losing side and fled. Such a fugitive's armor is called Fallen Samurai Armor. Its wearer was attacked while fleeing, so its back bristles with enemy arrows. They ran for their lives, with no time to pull them from armor or body.

Formal attire of the Kannagi, a sort of eastern Priest. Its sheer silken overgarment and faintly crimson cherry blossom embroidery are lovely. Some adventurers are said to become Kannagi out of longing for this outfit. And it's not only lovely: it also protects, making it a fine pick as armor too.

Lovely rose-adorned gauntlets only women who fight may wear. For whom does a lone rose blooming on the battlefield swing her sword? By this continent's custom, you don't get Rose Gauntlets yourself; they should be a gift from someone close to your heart. If you get some, give them to that someone!
A cloak dyed a refreshing blue. It has no special power, but its looks make it surprisingly popular. Some seasoned adventurers even wear this weak cloak on purpose, as a matter of taste.

A cloak that blesses those who find the path they must follow. Its defense is modest, but its spell resistance is strong. Even high-level adventurers are said to find it hard to part with. Some who lose the right to wear it can't bear to toss the cloak that saw them through their youth.

A tail yanked off a Tonafel. It protects its owner from sleep. It also serves as emergency rations: soak it in hot water and it will fill your belly a bit. But it is only emergency food; try as you might, it will never taste good.

A large flower that blooms deep in the forest, rather eerie-looking for a flower. Yet it has long been an offering to the gods and, despite its looks, is highly prized. Rolfan pollen blocks other pollens and scents, said to be one reason it became an offering.
An ember guarded by fire spirits; to obtain it, you must first win the spirits over. Elves can reportedly use this ember to craft special armor with high magic defense, a craft known only to elves.

The gem on a Carbuncle's brow. Beautiful and resistant to all sorts of magic, it was once so popular that Carbuncles were overhunted, nearly to extinction. Things have calmed down now, but they still threaten fiercely when humans approach.

Down of the Phoenix, famed as immortal. It strongly boosts and resists fire magic, but you must defeat a Phoenix to get it, so it's very rare. Beyond magic, it may stuff the pillows and quilts of the very rich: light and wonderfully warm, far beyond any common down quilt.

This egg is a delicacy, on almost everyone's list of 'foods to try before I die.' To get one, just take an egg from an Emperor Bird's nest. But a parent guarding its young fights beyond its strength, so don't take it lightly.

A jade ring famed for having no seam, a showcase of craftsmanship. With no seam, the gem's magic circulates almost forever, multiplying its power two- and threefold. Elves named this the 'Bole Effect,' and many rings use it. As armor, it wards off minor ailments.

A candy that soothes the throat. Suck one and your voice comes right back. It works wonders and tastes great, so you'll keep reaching for one when your mouth is bored. Watch out: they're often gone just when you need them! If you can't resist, let another adventurer carry them.

An herb that calms the confused. Just tear off a leaf and let them smell it; the scent will restore their composure. But beware: let them sniff every leaf at once, and they'll go past calm into apathy.
It cures charm. It's a genuine medicinal crystal, but who on earth gave it this name? Middle-aged adventurers find it rather embarrassing to buy.
A scroll holding a sleep spell. Use it to grant your foes a peaceful sleep. It is sometimes used as a cure for insomnia, too.
A scroll holding a light spell. Use it to brighten even the darkest dungeon.
A scroll that guides spirits and undead monsters to where they belong. Use it to break the curses on spirits and undead monsters and purify them.
A scroll holding a levitation spell. Use it to float every member of your party in the air, letting you walk even where there is no floor.

A scroll holding an escape spell. Use it and pure white smoke gushes from it, hiding the users from sight. The spell is magic, but the smoke is real: take the scroll out first! Use it lazily in your pocket and the air pressure will rip your clothes.

A scroll holding the power of breath. Use it and flames burst from the scroll at your foes, as powerful as a dragon's breath. It is meant to breathe fire, but not if the user has a different breath element.
A scroll holding a spell that briefly lifts range limits. Use it and your whole party's attack range becomes infinite, so now you can hit foes who felt safe out of reach.
A scroll holding a spell that raises evasion to a set level. Use it, and even the clumsiest start nimbly dodging attacks.
A scroll holding a spell that blocks level drain. Use it and a drain barrier appears before you, blocking an enemy drain attack once.
A scroll holding a spell that blocks breath. Use it and a breath barrier appears before you, blocking an enemy breath attack once.
